decisions.reason: 까발리다 here is spoiling the identity tease; “gives the game away” is more idiomatic for that banter than the stiffer “exposes someone.”
“Eyes went wide” naturalizes 눈을 크게 떴다, but SOL’s “finally” is not in 깨달은; BASE keeps the body-part calque.
decisions.replacement: Temur and Chinggen realized who the middle-aged man was, and their eyes went wide.

decisions.reason: 시원스럽게 is a brisk, unforced nod; “readily” matches that better than the heavier “without hesitation.”
혀를 내두르다 is the astonishment idiom, not a tongue-click; SOL invents that gesture and a “disbelief” coloring.
SOL’s “directed a look of doubt” is a calque of 눈빛을 던졌다; BASE’s “looked…suspiciously” is natural for 의구심 어린 눈빛.
넉살을 떨던 is shameless cheek, not mere “joking around”; SOL’s “as ever” adds a habit the source does not state.
decisions.replacement: Still being shameless, Black Sand went on.

decisions.reason: “All the more so” keeps 더더욱 그랬다 on the blood-boil; SOL’s singular “clan’s” is wrong for two chieftains, while BASE recasts it as “more powerful.”
decisions.replacement: The very word made their blood boil. All the more so for two young, strong chieftains who dreamed of restoring their clans to glory.

decisions.reason: 딱딱하게 굳은 is “hardened”; BASE’s “dried” is an extra detail the Korean does not give.
성(城) is the city already used in P78 and later 성을 침범; “stronghold” narrows it without support.
“Raiding” matches 습격, and the semicolon keeps the bandit/rebel contrast without the extra “would.”
사백에 달했소 is “amounted to four hundred,” not “nearly four hundred.”
입만 살았군 is empty boasting (“all talk”), not merely “a big mouth.”
BASE invents “what could they do?”; SOL replaces 해치우다 with “strike.” Keep SOL’s proposal rhythm with “finish the job.”
decisions.replacement: “We just have to finish the job like a bolt of lightning—too fast for anyone to react.”

decisions.reason: ……뭐? is one shocked utterance, not a separate silent “…” beat.
“…What?” restores the single source line BASE had split into two paragraphs.
“Came to three hundred, easily” is the natural reading of 삼백 명은 우습다; “commanded” matches 휘하 병력.
Glossary 무공 is “martial arts”; BASE’s “inferior martial arts to him” is unidiomatic, and SOL’s “ranked” / “martial skill” drift.
decisions.replacement: According to the Human Butcher, who had personally met the dead Pung Yang, no one here had weaker martial arts than he did.

decisions.reason: 노강호 is a formidable veteran, not an “old hand”; BASE’s appositive keeps that register without SOL’s weaker gloss.
